Coding Standards

Reference for VBA, Power Query (M), SQL, Oracle, Python, PySpark, DAX and automation flows. It applies to all code that is written or reviewed.

1. Principles

  • Maintainable first: clean, modular and idempotent (running it twice gives the same result).
  • No silently swallowed errors and no silent defaults: anything missing or invalid must be visible. A value that cannot be read becomes null and is counted separately, never 0.
  • Complete blocks, ready to copy and paste, with no "..." left to fill in.
  • Language: names and code in English; explanations in the asker's language.
  • Existing files: when modifying one, its style wins over these rules.

3. VBA

  • Option Explicit on the first line of every module.
  • On Error GoTo ErrorHandler. The handler restores Application and says what failed.
  • On Error Resume Next wraps a single line only, followed by On Error GoTo 0.
  • Section banners, in this order: Variable Declaration → Application Settings → logic → Restore Application Settings.
  • Application settings: ScreenUpdating, Calculation (xlCalculationManual) and EnableEvents are turned off, and always restored, including in the handler.
  • Names: descriptive PascalCase variables (CurrentWorkbook, CurrentTable). Work with ListObject, not fixed ranges.
Option Explicit

Sub ProcessInventoryData()
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler

    '================================================================
    ' Variable Declaration
    '================================================================
    Dim CurrentTable As ListObject

    '================================================================
    ' Application Settings
    '================================================================
    Application.ScreenUpdating = False
    Application.Calculation = xlCalculationManual
    Application.EnableEvents = False

    ' Processing logic

CleanExit:
    '================================================================
    ' Restore Application Settings
    '================================================================
    Application.ScreenUpdating = True
    Application.Calculation = xlCalculationAutomatic
    Application.EnableEvents = True
    Exit Sub

ErrorHandler:
    MsgBox "Error " & Err.Number & ": " & Err.Description, vbCritical
    Resume CleanExit
End Sub

4. Power Query (M)

  • Step names: English, CamelCase, short and descriptive (CleanedHeaders, FilteredRows, ChangedTypes). Never #"Changed Type1".
  • No blank lines between steps inside let ... in.
  • Comments: do not comment every step; the step name is the documentation. One description line at the top.
  • Query folding: filter and remove columns early to preserve it.
  • Culture arguments: none in conversions unless truly needed.
// Cleans the MB52 export and keeps unrestricted stock by plant
let
    Source = Csv.Document(File.Contents(FilePath), [Delimiter = ";", Encoding = 65001]),
    PromotedHeaders = Table.PromoteHeaders(Source, [PromoteAllScalars = true]),
    CleanedHeaders = Table.TransformColumnNames(PromotedHeaders, Text.Trim),
    FilteredRows = Table.SelectRows(CleanedHeaders, each [Plant] <> null)
in
    FilteredRows

5. SQL

  • CTEs (WITH) instead of nested subqueries, each with a clear intent.
  • Descriptive aliases for tables and columns (inv_head, fact_ord, po_line). Never a, b or t1.
  • Explicit columns: no SELECT * in anything delivered.
  • Layout: one clause per line, with explicit, aligned joins.
  • Nulls: handled explicitly with COALESCE or NVL, depending on the engine.

6. Oracle (EBS, Blitz Report)

  • No comment before the first statement. It causes ORA-24374: define not done before fetch or execute. The query starts directly with SELECT or WITH.
  • No trailing ";".
  • Documentation: if needed, the comment goes inside the query, after SELECT or WITH, or outside the file that gets executed.
  • Heavy queries run only inside the window agreed with the DBA.
WITH open_po AS (
    -- Open purchase order lines by item
    SELECT po_line.item_id,
           SUM(po_line.quantity) AS ordered_qty
    FROM   po_lines_all po_line
    WHERE  NVL(po_line.closed_code, 'OPEN') = 'OPEN'
    GROUP  BY po_line.item_id
)
SELECT item_mst.segment1 AS item_number,
       COALESCE(open_po.ordered_qty, 0) AS ordered_qty
FROM   mtl_system_items_b item_mst
LEFT   JOIN open_po ON open_po.item_id = item_mst.inventory_item_id
WHERE  item_mst.organization_id = :org_id

7. Python and pandas

  • ETL: pandas + pyarrow, with .parquet output.
  • Environment: one virtual environment per project, with declared dependencies.
  • Configuration (paths, tables, expected columns) lives outside the code.
  • Logging: logging instead of print, with a final completion message.
  • Section banners.
  • Error handling: try / except with a visible error around every file read and folder scan.
# ===============================================
# Validate Schema
# ===============================================
expected_columns = ["PO_NUM", "VENDOR_NUM", "ITEM_NUM", "QUANTITY", "NEED_BY_DATE"]
missing = [c for c in expected_columns if c not in df.columns]
if missing:
    raise ValueError(f"Missing columns: {missing}")

8. PySpark in Fabric: traps that already cost us

TrapWhat happensHow to do it right
NULL == "x" inside a filterIt returns NULL, not False, and the filter drops the row. A whole table can come out nearly empty.F.col(c).eqNullSafe("x"), or COALESCE before comparing.
Row has no .get()AttributeError: get, without saying where..asDict() when building dictionaries from collect() or first().
spark.table("name") without an attached lakehouseFails when run from a pipeline. Its sibling spark.catalog.tableExists() silently returns False, and the process continues without the table.Read by path: spark.read.format("delta").load(f"{base_path}/Tables/{name}").
Join alias plus several withColumn callsA new column with the same name shadows the aliased one, which stops resolving midway through the chain.Prefix columns before joining instead of qualifying with aliases.
sorted() with None after collect()TypeError between NoneType and str. Filtering the nulls out silently drops them from the catalog.Set nulls aside before sorting and append them at the end: key=lambda x: (x is None, x or "").
mssparkutils.fs.headSilently truncates at 100 KB, even if more is requested.open() from /lakehouse/default/..., and compare the bytes read against the file size.
option("wholetext", True)option() expects a string: the bool is ignored and only one line is read.Read with open() from the local mount.
OneLake pathsThey are case-sensitive.List the folder before writing the path into the config.
Missing field in a rowr["X"] on a missing column raises an error that only shows the name.Before reading field by field, check that the DataFrame has the columns; if not, say which ones it does have.

Safety net: when a process splits rows into buckets, check that the buckets add up to the input, and abort if they do not.

if n_rejected + n_invoiced + output != input_rows:
    raise ValueError(f"Rows lost: input {input_rows:,}, "
                     f"buckets {n_rejected + n_invoiced + output:,}")

Aligning schemas across sources: unionByName(other, allowMissingColumns=True).

9. DAX

  • Names: readable business names (Schedule Adherence %).
  • Steps: one VAR per step, and DIVIDE() instead of /.
  • Model: star schema, with measures in a measures table.
Schedule Adherence % =
VAR PlannedQty = SUM ( FactSchedule[PlannedQty] )
VAR AdheredQty = SUMX ( FactSchedule, MIN ( FactSchedule[ActualQty], FactSchedule[PlannedQty] ) )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( AdheredQty, PlannedQty )

10. Automation flows

  • Design order: Trigger → Actions → Conditions → Outputs → Error handling.
  • Connections: reusable, least-privilege.
  • Loops: no unnecessary ones.
  • Idempotency and retries made explicit.
  • Credentials: never inside the flow; they live in the connection.

11. Git

  • Direct push to main, done by Haz by hand.
  • Commit messages in Spanish, imperative, saying what changed.
  • Never AI tool signatures (Co-Authored-By, "Generated with").
  • Bypassing locks is forbidden: --no-verify, git add -f, disabling hooks.
